items.title: A Cameron–Martin shift cannot increase centered Gaussian ball mass
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, the Hahn–Banach theorem, and countable choice. Let $B$ be a real separable Banach space, and let $W$ be a centered Borel Gaussian random element with Borel law $\mu$. Let $C:B^*\to B$ be its covariance operator, let $E$ be the completion of $B^*/\ker C$ with inner product $\langle[\ell],[m]\rangle_E=m(C\ell)$, and let $i:E\to B$ be the canonical injection extending $[\ell]\mapsto C\ell$. For every $h\in E$ and $r>0$,
$$ \mu\bigl(\{x\in B:\|x-ih\|_B\le r\}\bigr)\le \mu\bigl(\{x\in B:\|x\|_B\le r\}\bigr). $$

references.title: E. Giné and R. Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models
references.locator: §2.4, Lemma 2.4.4 and Theorem 2.4.5, including the complete proof of the Banach Gaussian Anderson inequality.

references.title: M. Dashti, A. M. Stuart, and J. Voss, MAP Estimators and Their Consistency in Bayesian Nonparametric Inverse Problems
references.locator: §3, Theorem 3.2 proof, including the Gaussian small-ball shift comparison cited there; the finite-projection argument is supplied locally.

items.axiom_use: The finite-dimensional Gaussian-centering supplier assumes AC. The countable norming family uses HB and countable choice; AC implies countable choice. No stronger choice principle is used.

items.title: Small-ball ratios for Cameron–Martin translates of a Banach Gaussian
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, the Hahn–Banach theorem, and countable choice. Let $B$ be a real separable Banach space, and let $W$ be a centered Borel Gaussian random element with law $\mu$. Define its covariance by $C\ell=\mathbb E[\ell(W)W]$ for $\ell\in B^*$, let $N=\{\ell:\mathbb E[\ell(W)^2]=0\}$, and let $E$ be the completion of $B^*/N$ with inner product $\langle[\ell],[m]\rangle_E=\mathbb E[\ell(W)m(W)]$. Let $i:E\to B$ be the canonical injection extending $[\ell]\mapsto C\ell$. For $z\in B$ and $r>0$, write $\overline B_B(z,r)=\{x\in B:\|x-z\|_B\le r\}$. Then for any $h_1,h_2\in E$,
$$ \frac{\mu(\overline B_B(ih_1,r))}{\mu(\overline B_B(ih_2,r))} \longrightarrow \exp\!\left(\frac{\|h_2\|_E^2-\|h_1\|_E^2}{2}\right) \qquad(r\downarrow0). $$
The denominator is positive for every $r>0$.

references.title: M. Dashti, A. M. Stuart, and J. Voss, MAP Estimators and Their Consistency in Bayesian Nonparametric Inverse Problems
references.locator: §3, Theorem 3.2 and complete proof; its proof invokes the Gaussian small-ball ratio rather than proving it.

references.title: E. Kekkonen and P. Korolev, Inverse Problems, lecture notes
references.locator: §7.4, Theorem 7.5.3 and its stated Cameron–Martin ratio; the local argument supplies the ratio proof.

items.axiom_use: AC is required by the stated Gaussian Cameron–Martin and support interfaces. The approximation and limiting argument adds no stronger choice principle.

items.title: Small-ball MAP conventions and Cameron–Martin relative modes
items.statement:
Let $B$ be a separable Banach space with norm $\|\cdot\|_B$, and let $\Pi$ be a Borel probability measure on $B$. For $z\in B$ and $r>0$, write $\overline B_B(z,r)=\{u\in B:\|u-z\|_B\le r\}$ and $m_r(z)=\Pi(\overline B_B(z,r))$. A **strong small-ball MAP** is a point $z\in B$ for which
$$ \frac{m_r(z)}{\sup_{x\in B}m_r(x)}\longrightarrow1\qquad(r\downarrow0). $$
Assume AC for the covariance-induced Cameron–Martin notation. If $\Pi$ is a posterior law formed by weighting a centered Gaussian prior $\Pi_0$ on $B$, let $C\ell=\int_B\ell(u)u\,\Pi_0(du)$ be its covariance operator and let $E$ be the completion of $B^*/\ker C$ with inner product $\langle[\ell],[m]\rangle_E=m(C\ell)$; the canonical injection $i:E\to B$ extends $[\ell]\mapsto C\ell$. A **Cameron–Martin ratio mode** is a point $ih\in iE$ such that, for every $k\in E$, the denominator is positive for all sufficiently small $r$ and
$$ \lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{m_r(ih)}{m_r(ik)} $$
exists and is at least $1$. This pairwise comparison over fixed Cameron–Martin centers does not assert the global strong small-ball MAP condition.

For every $r>0$, $\sup_{x\in B}m_r(x)>0$: a countable dense subset gives a countable cover of $B$ by radius-$r$ open balls, each contained in its corresponding closed ball, and countable subadditivity rules out all such closed balls having zero probability.

references.title: M. Dashti, A. M. Stuart, and J. Voss, MAP Estimators and Their Consistency in Bayesian Nonparametric Inverse Problems
references.locator: §2, Definitions 2.1–2.3 for strong/generalized MAP notions; §3, Definition 3.1 for the Onsager–Machlup functional.

references.title: E. Kekkonen and P. Korolev, Inverse Problems, lecture notes
references.locator: §7.4, Definition 7.5.1 and Theorems 7.5.2–7.5.3 for small-ball and Onsager–Machlup conventions.

items.axiom_use: The global strong-mode definition is choice-free; AC is assumed only for the covariance-induced Cameron–Martin notation in the relative-mode branch.

items.title: Gaussian posterior small-ball ratios and the Onsager–Machlup functional
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, the Hahn–Banach theorem, and countable choice. Let $B$ be a real separable Banach space, and let $W$ be a centered Borel Gaussian random element in $B$ with law $\mu$. Define its covariance by $C\ell=\mathbb E[\ell(W)W]$ for $\ell\in B^*$, let $N=\{\ell:\mathbb E[\ell(W)^2]=0\}$, and let $E$ be the completion of $B^*/N$ with inner product $\langle[\ell],[m]\rangle_E=\mathbb E[\ell(W)m(W)]$. Write $i:E\to B$ for the canonical injection extending $[\ell]\mapsto C\ell$. Under AC, the image of the closed $E$-unit ball is compact in the $B$ norm. Let $\Phi:B\to\mathbb R$ be Borel measurable, locally bounded above, and locally Lipschitz. Suppose that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $M_\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$ \Phi(u)\ge M_\varepsilon-\varepsilon\|u\|_B^2\qquad(u\in B). $$
Define the evidence $Z=\int_B e^{-\Phi(u)}\,\mu(du)$ and, when $0<Z<\infty$, the posterior $\Pi(du)=Z^{-1}e^{-\Phi(u)}\mu(du)$. Then $0<Z<\infty$. For $h\in E$, define
$$ I(ih)=\Phi(ih)+\frac12\|h\|_E^2, \qquad I(u)=+\infty\quad(u\notin iE). $$
The functional $I$ attains a finite minimum on $iE$, and for every fixed $h_1,h_2\in E$,
$$ \frac{\Pi(\overline B_B(ih_1,r))}{\Pi(\overline B_B(ih_2,r))} \longrightarrow \exp\!\bigl(I(ih_2)-I(ih_1)\bigr) \qquad(r\downarrow0). $$
Its minimizers are exactly the Cameron–Martin ratio modes. This pairwise result makes no claim of a global strong small-ball MAP.

references.title: M. Dashti, A. M. Stuart, and J. Voss, MAP Estimators and Their Consistency in Bayesian Nonparametric Inverse Problems
references.locator: §2, Assumption 2.1; §3, Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.2 and complete proof; §3.3, Theorem 3.5 and §3.4, Corollary 3.10.

references.title: E. Kekkonen and P. Korolev, Inverse Problems, lecture notes
references.locator: §7.4, Theorems 7.5.2–7.5.3 and their proofs/statements; §7.5, Theorem 7.5.6 and complete compact-embedding minimizer proof.

items.axiom_use: AC supplies the Gaussian, compactness, and Fernique interfaces. HB and countable choice are hypotheses of the finite-projection ratio proof. The compactness-based minimizer argument uses a real bounded-sequence subsequence only; no global strong MAP is inferred from the pairwise ratio theorem.

title: Small-ball MAP and Cameron–Martin geometry — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Finite-dimensional small-ball MAP equals the density mode
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Take the parameter space and prior domain to be $B=D=\mathbb R^d$ with the Euclidean norm. Let $d,m\ge1$, let $C$ and $\Gamma$ be symmetric positive-definite real matrices of sizes $d\times d$ and $m\times m$, let $A$ be an $m\times d$ real matrix, and observe the fixed datum $y=Au+\eta$ with prior $u\sim N(0,C)$ and independent noise $\eta\sim N(0,\Gamma)$. Define $\Phi_y(u)=\tfrac12(y-Au)^T\Gamma^{-1}(y-Au)$ and $I_y(u)=\Phi_y(u)+\tfrac12u^TC^{-1}u$. The posterior has a positive continuous Lebesgue density proportional to $e^{-I_y(u)}$; its density mode is the unique minimizer of $I_y$ and is a strong small-ball MAP.

references.title: M. Dashti, A. M. Stuart, and J. Voss, MAP Estimators and Their Consistency in Bayesian Nonparametric Inverse Problems
references.locator: §2, finite-dimensional density definition and motivation; §3, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2.

references.title: E. Kekkonen and P. Korolev, Inverse Problems, lecture notes
references.locator: §7.4, Theorems 7.5.2–7.5.3 for the finite-dimensional and Gaussian small-ball relation.

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed for the repository's nondegenerate multivariate normal and density interfaces. The ball-average limit itself is elementary and choice-free.

items.title: An infinite-dimensional Gaussian has no locally finite translation-invariant density reference
items.statement: Every centered Borel Gaussian probability on an infinite-dimensional separable Banach space has a density with respect to some nonzero translation-invariant Borel measure that is finite on every bounded Borel set.

references.title: M. Dashti, A. M. Stuart, and J. Voss, MAP Estimators and Their Consistency in Bayesian Nonparametric Inverse Problems
references.locator: §2, discussion of the absence of an infinite-dimensional Lebesgue density; §3, Definition 3.1.

references.title: E. Giné and R. Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models
references.locator: §2.4, Banach Gaussian measures and Cameron–Martin geometry; §4.4.1, Gaussian series in infinite-dimensional function spaces.

items.axiom_use: AC and countable choice are assumed for the Gaussian-series supplier. The nonexistence argument uses an explicit countable set and countable subadditivity only.

items.title: The posterior mean need not be a small-ball MAP
items.statement: Let $\theta$ have the uniform prior on $[0,1]$, regarded as a Borel probability on $\mathbb R$, and let an observation $Y\in\{0,1\}$ satisfy $\mathbb P(Y=1\mid\theta)=\theta^2(1-\theta)$. After observing $Y=1$, the posterior has density $12\theta^2(1-\theta)$ on $[0,1]$ and zero outside. Its unique density mode, at $\theta=2/3$, is a strong small-ball MAP, while its posterior mean is $3/5$. Thus the posterior mean and a small-ball MAP differ.

references.title: M. Dashti, A. M. Stuart, and J. Voss, MAP Estimators and Their Consistency in Bayesian Nonparametric Inverse Problems
references.locator: §2, Definitions 2.1–2.3, distinguishing MAP estimators from posterior expectations.

references.title: E. Kekkonen and P. Korolev, Inverse Problems, lecture notes
references.locator: §7.4, Definition 7.5.1 and the discussion following Theorem 7.5.3.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the prior, likelihood, evidence and posterior calculations are explicit on the real line.
